content: The efficacy and safety of Desloratadine Tablets, 5 mg once daily, were evaluated in a clinical study involving 416 patients with chronic idiopathic urticaria, aged between 12 and 84 years. Among these participants, 211 received Desloratadine. In two double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized clinical trials lasting six weeks, Desloratadine Tablets significantly reduced the severity of pruritus compared to placebo at the pre-specified one-week primary time point evaluation. Secondary endpoints were also assessed, and during the first week of therapy, Desloratadine Tablets, 5 mg, demonstrated a reduction in the Number of Hives and the Size of the Largest Hive compared to placebo. The clinical safety of Desloratadine Oral Solution was established in three 15-day, double-blind, placebo-controlled safety studies conducted in pediatric subjects. These studies included children with a documented history of allergic rhinitis, chronic idiopathic urticaria, or those who were candidates for antihistamine therapy. Desloratadine Oral Solution, 5 mg, was administered to 60 pediatric subjects aged 6 to 11 years. A dose of 2.5 mg was given to 55 pediatric subjects aged 2 to 5 years, and 0.5 mg was administered to 66 pediatric subjects aged 6 to 11 months. The results of these studies confirmed the safety of Desloratadine Oral Solution in pediatric patients aged 6 months to 11 years. Desloratadine Oral Solution is available in a concentration of 5 mg/1 mL and is packaged in 16-ounce and 4-ounce amber glass bottles (NDC 0085-1334-01 and NDC 0085-1334-02, respectively). It should be stored at 25°C (77°F). Patients should be instructed to use Desloratadine as directed. Since food does not affect the bioavailability of the medication, Desloratadine Tablets, Oral Solution, or RediTabs Tablets may be taken with or without meals. Patients should be advised not to increase the dose or dosing frequency, as studies have not shown increased effectiveness at higher doses, and somnolence may occur. For patients with phenylketonuria, it is important to note that Desloratadine RediTabs Tablets contain phenylalanine. The interaction between alcohol and Desloratadine has not been established. Patients should consult their healthcare provider regarding the effects of consuming alcohol while taking this medication. Desloratadine is marketed under the brand names Clarinex and Clarinex RediTabs. There is limited information available regarding look-alike drug names for Desloratadine in the drug label.
